name: Extended NYT Connections
ability_definition: The ability to generate or use different sets of rules for combining or grouping things in different ways.

task_realism.reasoning: The core operation does exercise the ability: partitioning items under several competing rules and dropping tempting wrong groupings. But the tasks are recreational word puzzles built around trivia, wordplay, homophones and hidden words. Workplace regrouping looks different. Examples are re-segmenting customers, reclassifying inventory, building taxonomies, or re-framing cases by different criteria, all tied to a purpose and to domain knowledge.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The setup is prompt-only with no tools and no stakes. Each puzzle has a single designer-intended answer, and the distribution is curated, deliberately adversarial and self-contained. Real work involves open-ended, ambiguous item sets with no guaranteed correct partition. Groupings are judged by usefulness rather than by an answer key, and they are revised over time with feedback and outside information.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It captures a meaningful slice of the ability: several rule types per puzzle, and resistance to red herrings (fixation and Einstellung), which the extra decoy words strengthen. It is limited to lexical and semantic categories in a fixed 4x4 structure. It does not test generating new grouping schemes for a goal, handling non-verbal or quantitative attributes, or choosing how many groups or which dimensions matter.

format_match.reasoning: The input is a list of isolated words and the output is four labeled sets with a fixed size. This is an artificial puzzle format. Real artifacts would be datasets, documents, case files or product lists, organized into schemas, reports or classification systems whose structure the worker defines.

transferability_reasoning: Extended Connections isolates a real part of Category Flexibility: switching among grouping rules and overriding misleading surface associations. That makes it the best available proxy. However, its word-puzzle content, single answer key and fixed format differ sharply from open-ended, purpose-driven categorization at work, so strong scores say only modestly more than that a model resists lexical red herrings.

2025.metric: Percent score (mean share of correct groups per puzzle, with the linear partial credit used in 2025)
2025.human_reference: General educated adults who do word and category puzzles (typical NYT Connections players), used as a proxy for people applying category flexibility in work settings
